newsitem.title: UK: BAe shares gain on defence alliance hopes.
newsitem.headline: BAe shares gain on defence alliance hopes.

text.p: Shares in British Aerospace gained 1.7 percent on Monday on a report that Britain's Ministry of Defence has dropped its opposition to a defence-equipment alliance between BAe and GEC.
BAe shares touched an intraday high of 1,167p in early trade on Monday before easing slightly to 1,165-1/1p by 0913 GMT, up 19-1/2p on the day. The broader market was up 0.32 percent.

The Sunday Times newspaper reported that the ministry was prepared to accept a deal because of a series of recent developments, including the accelerating pace of restructuring in the global defence industry.
BAe dismissed the report as speculation but dealers said it had lifted the shares.
Brian Newman, analyst at Henderson Crosthwaite, said the report highlighted the moves to what he called the broader European horizon for the defence market.

"We think defence markets are very strong at the moment and the Middle East is benefitting from the high price of oil...the aerospace sector is still one where the short and medium term prospects look excellent," he said.
Newman said he continued to recommend BAe as a "buy".
